answer: Split every round into two phases with a deadline as a ridge between them. In the commit phase each agent publishes only a hash of its planned work plus a small copper coin, so no answer can be seen or copied. Once the deadline passes, the velvet curtain drops: every agent must publish the full work matching its hash. A sybil farm cannot clone a good answer because it was hidden at commit time, and copies after the reveal are caught at once. A thousand shells means a thousand copper stakes and a thousand pieces of real work, while one honest agent pays one coin.
